sources.title: e-Visas for certain countries
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs, Defence, Development Cooperation and Foreign Trade, Luxembourg
sources.officialityEvidence: The actual Luxembourg Government page opened successfully. It has a 7 January 2026 update date and names Ukraine immediately below the sentence expressly addressing Luxembourg nationals. It is not merely a generic directory of eVisa portals, but it supplies no Ukrainian legal basis or nationality-specific eligibility determination.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Luxembourg nationals can no longer obtain a tourist visa on arrival, but need to apply for an "e-Tourist Visa" before their travel

sources.title: Ukraine EU accession questionnaire response, Volume 5, Chapters XXII-XXV: historical visa requirements and EU-citizen entry
sources.publisher: Government of Ukraine, European Integration Portal
sources.officialityEvidence: The actual 674-page PDF opened on the Cabinet of Ministers' official European Integration Portal. PDF pages 84-86 describe the EU-citizen waiver under Decree 1131/2005; pages 161 and 165 identify the nationality table as updated 17 April 2022 and explicitly place Luxembourg in the ordinary-passport visa-free cohort. This is accessible historical evidence, not proof of a September 2026 rule.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Luxembourg visa-free stay for up to 90 days within 180 days

conflicts.officialStatus: unresolved: issuer e-Tourist Visa statement is unreconciled with destination-government historical ordinary-passport waiver evidence
conflicts.explanation: The issuer page expressly addresses Luxembourg nationals and lists Ukraine; the possibility that it was merely a generic portal link was checked and not supported by its actual wording. However, that page alone does not establish Ukrainian eVisa eligibility. Ukraine's accessible accession response expressly documents a 2022 ordinary-passport waiver, while the operative decree and current MFA entry table could not be retrieved. No current replacement category is established.

unresolved.reason: Current ordinary-passport visitor treatment is not established. The accessible Luxembourg guidance explicitly prescribes a pre-travel e-Tourist Visa for Ukraine, but the linked visa service did not yield a nationality-specific rule. A newly opened official Ukrainian accession-response PDF affirmatively documents the EU waiver and Luxembourg ordinary-passport 90/180 treatment as of 17 April 2022; it cannot prove present force. Direct current-decree and destination-MFA retrievals failed, so neither legal repeal nor present waiver operation is inferred from those failures.
